title: QCLI-266's fix is landed on dev and unreleased, so every consumer still runs the broken help
description:
Filed fresh at the orchestrator's ruling rather than by reopening QCLI-266: a Done record is history and stays, and this task is the truth about the shipped package.

QCLI-266 ('help and manifest do not tell a first-time caller how to write a valid task create') was closed Done on 2026-09-11 with all four acceptance criteria checked. The fix is real and it is on dev. No consumer can get it.

Verified 2026-09-11:

  src/application/command-parameters.ts            exists on dev, mtime 2026-09-11 07:50
  grep -c 'command-parameters|valueSyntax' on the installed bundle   -> 0
  npm view @opum-ai/quest versions                 -> ["0.5.0", "0.6.0"]
  npm view @opum-ai/quest dist-tags                -> latest = 0.6.0
  node -p require('./package.json').version        -> 0.6.0

So 0.6.0 is the latest published version AND it predates the fix, while dev's package.json still reads 0.6.0. This is a release gap, not a regression -- but the version string cannot express the difference, which is why it is invisible: `quest --version` reports 0.6.0 for the shipped package and for a dev checkout carrying commits the shipped package does not have. Nothing a caller can run distinguishes them.

How this surfaced, which is the part worth keeping: a session in THIS repository, with the fixed source on disk, hit the exact failure QCLI-266 describes -- three consecutive 'task create received invalid arguments' rejections before working out that --acceptance-criteria takes a single JSON array string and cannot be repeated. It read `quest help task create`, which listed the flag name and said nothing about its value shape, because the binary on PATH is the npm-published 0.6.0. The repository is not a witness to its own fixes.

That is the same class as QCLI-269's second half and as the reported OMARK-42 traps: a surface that a caller reasonably trusts reporting something that is not true of the thing they are actually running.

Scope is a patch release off dev. The provenance gate from QCLI-267 (scripts/qualification/release-provenance.mjs, --pre before publishing) is already wired into the release workflow and must pass rather than be worked around; docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md carries the procedure. Publishing to a registry is in the fleet's irreversible set, so the publish step needs the user's direct authority, not an orchestrator's -- that approval is part of this task, not an obstacle to filing it.

Worth settling while here, since it is what made the gap silent: whether a dev checkout should report a version distinguishable from the last published one. Not a blocker for the release, and should not grow into one.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A published @opum-ai/quest version carries the QCLI-266 fix, verified by grepping the PUBLISHED bundle for the value-shape rendering, not by reading the repository source.
quest help task create, run from the published binary, states the value shape of --acceptance-criteria -- the exact gap that produced three rejections in-repo.
The QCLI-267 provenance gate passes on the release rather than being skipped, and the published version has a gitHead resolving to a commit that exists.
The publish step is authorised directly by the user, since registry publication is in the fleet irreversible set and an orchestrator decision does not cover it.

Whether a dev checkout should report a version distinguishable from the last published one is decided and recorded -- either implemented, or declined with the reason -- so the next such gap is visible from the version string.

plan: 1. Bump root + 6 platform package.json versions to 0.6.1
2. Turn CHANGELOG Unreleased section into a dated 0.6.1 entry, honestly labeled given QCLI-264/265 breaking changes
3. Run bun run check:packages / test:packages locally with pinned Bun 1.3.14
4. PR into dev, get source-gates green, squash merge
6. Confirm QCLI-267 provenance --pre gate passes, tag v0.6.1, dispatch prepublication-qualification.yml against the tag
8. Stage everything short of publish; ask my own user with AskUserQuestion to authorize the actual npm publish

HARD BLOCKER, host-specific, not a code defect: git cannot touch the freshly-built npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest (the one platform binary that is native-executable on THIS host) without the process being SIGKILLed. Reproduced identically across git status, git diff --stat, git add, and git hash-object scoped to that exact path -- all killed (exit 137), consistently, regardless of timeout (tried up to 300s) and with the tool sandbox explicitly disabled. Ruled out: file corruption (plain shasum -a 256 on the identical file succeeds instantly; cp+chmod+x+direct execution of a copy outside the repo all succeed and correctly print 0.6.1); OOM (plenty of free memory, and the other 5 platform binaries -- comparable size, same build step, same directory tree -- are added/diffed/hashed by git with no issue); sandbox-tool-imposed limit (identical result with dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true). Each killed git process also left a stale .git/index.lock; verified no live process held it (lsof empty, no git process in ps) before removing it. The pattern (only the host-native, newly-created, ad-hoc-signed executable; only when git itself touches it; never on a plain read) points at host security tooling intercepting git handling a new native executable, which I will not try to bypass. Escalating to my own user rather than working around it.

CORRECTION (caught by opum-agent before a PR was opened): the pushed branch chore/QCLI-271-release-0.6.1 (commit 1a203ac) does NOT have a hole for npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest -- it has the OLD 0.6.0 blob, unchanged (verified: blob 50d874fe4687f6781dc541140a8a4b4236e6b89a identical on origin/dev and origin/chore/QCLI-271-release-0.6.1). A tracked file a commit doesn't touch keeps its prior contents; it does not go missing. Since the release workflow publishes straight from npm/quest-<target>/ with no build step, merging as-is would silently ship the 0.6.0 executable under the @opum-ai/quest-darwin-arm64@0.6.1 name -- every gate that doesn't compare bytes would pass. No PR opened. Completion step at /Users/jdnewhouse/repos/quest-cli must REPLACE the file and confirm the blob sha actually CHANGES to 4e56fc67e5880fd630e000197cf928ceabaa80c66fc4891175243c39fbc16bcc (git ls-tree/hash-object after the commit) -- if the blob is still 50d874fe, the copy did nothing. Also worth a follow-up: a check that fails when any npm/*/bin/ blob is unchanged from the prior release while the version string moved -- nothing currently catches that class of defect.

It exists at /Volumes/external/repos/quest-cli/npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest (this checkout) and has ALSO already been copied onto disk at /Users/jdnewhouse/repos/quest-cli/npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest (confirmed via shasum -- correct bytes are there).
- BLOCKER, now confirmed on BOTH checkouts, not volume-specific as first hypothesized: git operations (status/diff/add/hash-object/commit) touching that exact file get SIGKILLed (exit 137) on /Volumes/external/repos/quest-cli, and git status -sb was also SIGKILLed on /Users/jdnewhouse/repos/quest-cli when checked. Root cause not identified -- looks like host security tooling reacting to git handling this specific native arm64 executable, but it is not simply 'external volume vs boot volume' as I first guessed. Do not attempt to bypass whatever this is (strip quarantine attrs, re-sign, disable a protection) without the user's explicit say-so.

Next step is the user's/orchestrator's call: likely identifying what's intercepting git on this specific file (both checkouts), or finding a checkout/machine where it genuinely does not happen, before finishing and reviewing this branch.

Reconfirmed in a fresh session, 2026-09-13, on this same checkout (/Volumes/external/repos/quest-cli), branch chore/QCLI-271-release-0.6.1 unchanged at 7e9a51f (matches origin, nothing new pushed to this branch): the SIGKILL blocker is real and WIDER than previously documented. Beyond git status/diff/add/hash-object on the flagged path itself, plain unscoped `git status`, `git commit` (even committing an unrelated, already-staged .quest/ file with no path touching npm/), and `git reset -- <unrelated-path>` all get SIGKILLed (exit 137) too -- apparently any operation that makes git refresh/rebuild the full index (which includes the dirty npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest entry) is affected, not only ones naming that path directly. Scoped git commands with explicit pathspecs excluding npm/ (git diff --stat -- <path>, git checkout -- <path> [flaky -- see below], git add <path>) generally still work. Worked around for unrelated .quest/ commits this session using pure plumbing that never refreshes the working-tree-wide index: git show HEAD:<path> + cp to revert a single file's content, and git update-index --cacheinfo <mode>,<sha>,<path> to unstage a single file -- both avoided the kill where git checkout -- <path> and git reset -- <path> intermittently either hung/got-killed (leaving a stale but genuinely-unheld .git/index.lock, verified via ps+lsof each time before removing) or silently no-op'd. Did not touch npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest itself, per the existing instruction not to bypass this without the user's say-so. Unrelated repo work this session (QCLI-252 fix+ship, a dev->main promotion) was done successfully by routing entirely through git worktrees off origin/dev (.claude/worktrees/<name>, cleaned up after), which never touch this checkout's dirty binary and were unaffected.
